chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from some of his companions, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: regarding

Concerning a slave and a free man who killed a free man, he said: “If he wishes, he may kill the free man; and if he wishes, he may kill the slave. And if he chooses to kill the free man, he strikes the two sides of the slave.”

key_terms.حُرٍّ: a free person; used for both the perpetrator and the victim in context
key_terms.رَجُلًا حُرًّا: a free man; the victim of the killing
key_terms.ضَرَبَ جَنْبَيِ الْعَبْدِ: he strikes the two sides of the slave; a corporal penalty mentioned in this ruling
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave; one of the two perpetrators in the case
key_terms.قَتَلَ الْحُرَّ: to execute the free perpetrator in retaliation
key_terms.قَتَلَ الْعَبْدَ: to execute the slave perpetrator in retaliation
key_terms.قَتَلَا: the two killed; indicates joint participation in the homicide

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave and a free man jointly kill a free man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning joint homicide committed by a slave and a free man against a free man. It outlines the options available in retaliation and distinguishes between the legal consequences applied to the free perpetrator and the slave.
